name: SolarZone HP
shortDescription: Hanita Coatings SolarZone HP is a high-performance solar control film delivering strong heat rejection and UV block for Philadelphia offices, rowhomes, and commercial properties across a range of VLT options.
description:
SolarZone HP is the flagship entry in Hanita Coatings' SolarZone solar control lineup — a sputtered metallized film designed for Philadelphia commercial and residential properties where solar heat gain, glare, and UV protection are the primary concerns. Available in a range of visible light transmission levels, SolarZone HP provides meaningful total solar energy rejection (TSER) without the heavily tinted or mirrored appearance of older-generation solar control films.

For Philadelphia Center City office buildings with south and west-facing glazing, SolarZone HP reduces peak summer cooling load, brings glare down to a level that makes workstations more comfortable, and blocks UV radiation that fades flooring, furniture, and merchandise. The film's sputtered metallic construction delivers consistent performance across the panel for the life of the installation.

Hanita Coatings is an Israeli manufacturer with decades of experience in high-performance architectural film, with installations at hospitals, universities, government facilities, and commercial properties worldwide. SolarZone HP brings that manufacturing quality to Philadelphia's mix of historic rowhomes, Class A office towers, and high-exposure commercial facades.

Window Film Philadelphia installs SolarZone HP across the full range of Philadelphia residential and commercial properties, selecting the appropriate VLT based on glass orientation, building type, and client priorities.

benefits.heading: High-Performance Solar Control
benefits.body: SolarZone HP's sputtered construction delivers effective TSER and heat rejection on Philadelphia south- and west-facing commercial glass, addressing peak summer cooling load.

benefits.heading: UV Fading Protection
benefits.body: Blocks UV radiation that damages flooring, furniture, artwork, and merchandise — a key concern for Philadelphia retailers, galleries, and premium residential interiors.

benefits.heading: Multiple VLT Options
benefits.body: Available from light to dark VLT levels, letting Philadelphia property managers match the film to glass orientation, HOA guidelines, and daylight preferences.

name: SolarZone XTRM
shortDescription: Hanita Coatings SolarZone XTRM is an extreme-performance spectrally selective solar control film — maximum heat rejection with high visible light transmission for Philadelphia Class A offices and high-exposure commercial facades.
description:
SolarZone XTRM is Hanita Coatings' highest-performance solar control specification — a spectrally selective film engineered to reject maximum solar heat while maintaining high visible light transmission. Spectrally selective construction targets the infrared and UV portions of the solar spectrum while allowing visible light to pass through, delivering the combination of bright interiors and meaningful heat control that demanding Philadelphia commercial specifications require.

For Center City Class A office towers, University City institutional buildings, and large commercial facades with significant south or west exposure, SolarZone XTRM is the right specification when a visible light reduction would compromise the building's daylight character or architectural standards. The XTRM delivers superior TSER with a near-neutral exterior appearance that doesn't impose a reflective or heavily tinted look on the building facade.

Installations at hotels, banks, technology campuses, and healthcare facilities worldwide validate SolarZone XTRM for demanding specifications. For Philadelphia commercial projects requiring performance documentation — TSER percentages, U-value improvement, shading coefficients — Hanita's technical data sheets and case studies support full specification submittal.

Window Film Philadelphia evaluates glass orientation, exposure, and performance goals before recommending SolarZone XTRM versus other SolarZone options.

benefits.heading: Spectrally Selective Technology
benefits.body: Targets infrared and UV wavelengths while passing visible light — Philadelphia offices get heat control without the dark or reflective appearance of conventional high-performance films.

benefits.heading: Maximum TSER
benefits.body: Extreme-specification heat rejection addresses the highest-demand south and west exposures in Philadelphia's commercial building stock without sacrificing daylighting quality.

benefits.heading: Specification-Ready
benefits.body: Full technical data sheet support for Philadelphia architectural and engineering firms — TSER, VLT, shading coefficient, and U-value data available for submittal documentation.

name: SkyLite Xtra
shortDescription: Hanita Coatings SkyLite Xtra is a high-clarity spectrally selective solar control film — designed for Philadelphia buildings where near-clear glass appearance is required alongside meaningful solar heat rejection.
description:
SkyLite Xtra is Hanita Coatings' high-clarity spectrally selective option — engineered for Philadelphia commercial and institutional properties where a near-clear exterior appearance is a design or code requirement, but solar heat control and UV protection are still priorities. The film's spectrally selective construction delivers meaningful TSER at VLT levels that read as essentially clear glass from the street — compatible with Philadelphia historic district guidelines, HOA restrictions, and curtain-wall architectural standards that prohibit reflective or tinted treatments.

For Penn Medicine clinic suites, University of Pennsylvania academic buildings, Center City historic facades, and any Philadelphia commercial property where the glass character must be preserved, SkyLite Xtra provides solar and UV protection without the aesthetic compromise. The film's low exterior reflectance means it doesn't impose a mirrored or heavily tinted appearance on buildings where that would conflict with neighborhood character or building regulations.

SkyLite Xtra appears in Hanita's case study portfolio in applications at retail malls, hospital complexes, and commercial headquarters where occupant comfort and daylighting both matter.

Window Film Philadelphia recommends SkyLite Xtra for south- and east-facing Philadelphia glass where both solar performance and visual clarity are specified requirements.

benefits.heading: Near-Clear Appearance
benefits.body: High VLT with low exterior reflectance — SkyLite Xtra meets Philadelphia historic district and HOA requirements that prohibit reflective or tinted glass treatments.

benefits.heading: Spectrally Selective Solar Control
benefits.body: Targets heat and UV without reducing visible light to levels that require lighting compensation — Philadelphia offices and institutions stay bright with meaningful solar protection.

benefits.heading: Institutional-Grade Specification
benefits.body: Used in hospitals, universities, and government facilities worldwide — supports specification documentation for Philadelphia institutional and commercial projects.

name: e-Lite Low-E
shortDescription: Hanita Coatings e-Lite is a low-emissivity solar control film — delivering year-round thermal improvement for Philadelphia rowhomes and commercial buildings needing both summer heat rejection and winter insulation.
description:
Hanita Coatings e-Lite is the low-emissivity film in the SolarZone lineup — engineered for year-round thermal performance in both directions, not just summer solar rejection. Like all low-E window films, e-Lite adds an insulating layer to existing single-pane or older glass that helps retain interior heat in winter while still rejecting solar gain in summer. For Philadelphia's IECC Climate Zone 4A mixed-humid climate, where genuine winters follow genuine summers, e-Lite addresses the thermal limitation of the city's large stock of older single-pane rowhome glass without requiring window replacement.

For Fishtown rowhomes, Society Hill historic windows, Chestnut Hill colonials, and any Philadelphia property with original or older single-pane glass, e-Lite adds meaningful thermal resistance that reduces both summer cooling load and winter heat loss. The visible light transmission is high — the film reads as clear or nearly clear glass from inside and outside, compatible with historic preservation guidelines and HOA requirements.

The e-Lite's low-emissivity construction is backed by Hanita's standard technical data, which documents both TSER (summer) and U-value improvement (winter). For Philadelphia properties trying to qualify for energy performance documentation or improvement rebates, e-Lite's dual-season credentials support the case.

Window Film Philadelphia recommends e-Lite for Philadelphia properties where year-round thermal performance, not just summer solar control, is the specification priority.

benefits.heading: Year-Round Thermal Performance
benefits.body: Low-emissivity construction improves both summer heat rejection and winter heat retention — the right fit for Philadelphia's Zone 4A mixed-humid, four-season climate.

benefits.heading: Single-Pane Upgrade
benefits.body: Adds meaningful thermal resistance to Philadelphia's large stock of older single-pane rowhome glass without the cost or preservation complications of window replacement.

benefits.heading: Near-Clear Appearance
benefits.body: High VLT keeps Philadelphia historic homes and residential interiors bright — compatible with historic district and HOA glass requirements.

name: SafetyZone
shortDescription: Hanita Coatings SafetyZone is a safety and security window film — designed to retain glass fragments after impact and delay forced entry on Philadelphia retail, school, government, and commercial glass.
description:
SafetyZone is Hanita Coatings' safety and security film — a polyester film applied to the interior glass surface that holds broken glass in place after impact, reducing laceration injury risk and significantly increasing the time required to penetrate treated glass. SafetyZone is available in clear and lightly tinted versions at multiple mil thicknesses, matching the performance level to the threat profile and application type.

For Philadelphia schools, government buildings, retail storefronts, and commercial properties where smash-and-grab deterrence or occupant safety is a priority, SafetyZone provides a passive, always-on protection layer. When glass breaks — from a storm impact, an accident, an attempted forced entry, or an explosion overpressure — SafetyZone holds the fragments in the frame, slowing penetration and reducing the scatter of glass shards into occupied areas.

Hanita's SafetyZone portfolio includes case studies at Philadelphia-adjacent properties, hospitals, government facilities, and retail centers worldwide. For commercial projects requiring performance documentation — blast ratings, impact testing, forced-entry delay specifications — Hanita's SafetyZone data sheets support specification-level submittals.

SafetyZone can be combined with SolarZone solar control or PolyZone decorative film for a layered specification that addresses both safety and solar performance in a single glass treatment. Window Film Philadelphia handles SafetyZone specification and installation across Philadelphia schools, retail, and commercial properties.

benefits.heading: Glass Fragment Retention
benefits.body: SafetyZone holds broken glass in place on impact — protecting Philadelphia occupants from laceration in storms, accidents, and forced-entry attempts.

benefits.heading: Forced-Entry Delay
benefits.body: Film-retained glass significantly increases penetration time — a meaningful deterrent for Philadelphia retail storefronts and school entrances facing smash-and-grab or intrusion risk.

benefits.heading: Multiple Thickness Options
benefits.body: Available at several mil thicknesses to match the application — standard safety glazing for schools and offices, or heavier-duty specifications for high-security Philadelphia government and commercial facilities.
